name: Autonomic Nervous System, Hypothalamus and Horner Syndrome

reference.source: Clinical Neuroanatomy Made Ridiculously Simple / Guyton and Hall
clinicalPearls: Sympathetic outflow originates from T1-L2 intermediolateral horn; parasympathetic from CN III, VII, IX, X and S2-S4
Lateral hypothalamus stimulates appetite; ventromedial nucleus promotes satiety; suprachiasmatic controls circadian rhythm
Oculosympathetic pathway is a 3-neuron chain: hypothalamus to ciliospinal center (C8-T2), to superior cervical ganglion, to iris
Horner syndrome triad: ptosis (superior tarsal muscle), miosis (dilator pupillae), and anhidrosis
Apical lung Pancoast tumor invading the sympathetic trunk is a classic cause of preganglionic Horner syndrome
reference.pathophysiology: The hypothalamus coordinates endocrine and autonomic homeostasis via neuroendocrine axes and descending autonomic projections. Disruption of the sympathetic chain at central (brainstem), preganglionic (thoracic inlet), or postganglionic (carotid canal) levels denervates ipsilateral ocular smooth muscle and facial sweat glands.
additionalInvestigations: Topical apraclonidine (0.5%) eye drop test for reversal of anisocoria confirming Horner syndrome
CT chest and neck with IV contrast to evaluate lung apex and carotid sheath
MRI brain and brainstem if central Horner syndrome suspected
